title: Rencontre à la salle de sport  (Meeting at the Gym)

segments.t: At an exclusive Parisian fitness club, Andréa tracks down renowned actor Fabrice Luchini on the workout machines. She delivers a passionate pitch to poach him for the ASK agency, but Luchini has his own unique philosophy. Let's listen to the scene in French first.
Bonjour, Fabrice! Tu viens souvent ici?
Je vous connais, vous êtes agent, non?
Andréa Martel, je travaille chez ASK.
Vous ne devriez pas être au bureau?
En fait, je suis au travail là.
Je suis là pour vous. Vous êtes un talent rare.
Qu'est-ce que vous proposez exactement?
Je propose un nouvel élan artistique.
Tout ça est un peu bizarre.
Débarquer dans une salle de sport pour me parler!
Je suis chez Bréhier depuis trente-cinq ans.
On est un vieux couple. Je l'aime bien.
La nouveauté est un concept qui ne m'intéresse pas.
Peut-être que vous voulez juste vous ennuyer.
Ne dites pas du mal de l'ennui.
Je vous laisse donc vous ennuyer avec Bréhier.
Let's explore the conversation line by line and unpack the French phrases.
Bonjour, Fabrice! Tu viens souvent ici?
'Hello, Fabrice! Do you come here often?' Andréa initiates the conversation with a friendly greeting. She uses the casual 'you'. In French, this is perfectly fine.
Je vous connais, vous êtes agent, non?
'I know you, you are an agent, right?' Fabrice uses the formal 'you' to guess her profession. A standard way to speak in French.
Andréa Martel, je travaille chez ASK.
'Andréa Martel, I work at ASK.' She uses a handy chunk meaning at the house of or at the office of. It is used for companies. In French, you will hear this.
Vous ne devriez pas être au bureau?
'Should you not be at the office?' Fabrice asks a question using a cognate meaning office or desk. The French say this often.
En fait, je suis au travail là.
'In fact, I am at work right now.' Andréa insists she is officially working, using a handy phrase meaning in fact. In French, this is quite common.
Je suis là pour vous. Vous êtes un talent rare.
'I am here for you. You are a rare talent.' She uses the formal 'you' to flatter him and show respect. This is how you say it in French.
Qu'est-ce que vous proposez exactement?
'What are you offering exactly?' Built from an action meaning to propose, Fabrice asks what she wants. He remains formal. A handy phrase in French.
Je propose un nouvel élan artistique.
'I offer a new artistic impetus.' This uses the descriptor meaning new to promise fresh creative energy. A useful expression in French.
Tout ça est un peu bizarre.
'All of this is a bit strange.' You'll hear this cognate used to describe something weird or odd. This is very typical in French.
Débarquer dans une salle de sport pour me parler!
'Turning up in a gym to speak to me!' Fabrice points out that arriving unannounced in a sports hall is highly unusual. A common chunk in French.
Je suis chez Bréhier depuis trente-cinq ans.
'I have been with Bréhier for thirty-five years.' Literally 'I am at Bréhier', this means he is a client there. He mentions his long history. You will hear this in French.
On est un vieux couple. Je l'aime bien.
'We are an old couple. I like him.' Fabrice uses a casual expression for we. He describes his deep bond with his agent. This is perfectly natural in French.
La nouveauté est un concept qui ne m'intéresse pas.
'Novelty is a concept that does not interest me.' Fabrice uses a cognate to reject trendy career shifts. In French, it works nicely.
Peut-être que vous voulez juste vous ennuyer.
'Maybe you just want to be bored.' Andréa uses an action meaning to bore oneself. She challenges his resistance with sarcasm. The French use this a lot.
Ne dites pas du mal de l'ennui.
'Do not speak ill of boredom.' Fabrice defends this existential state. He uses a phrase meaning to speak badly of. In French, it sounds perfect.
Je vous laisse donc vous ennuyer avec Bréhier.

'I leave you then to be bored with Bréhier.' Andréa concludes her exit with sharp wit, repeating the action meaning to bore oneself. This is standard in French. Now let's listen to the entire dialogue once more to lock in what you have learned.

Andréa's bold fitness ambush ends with Luchini standing loyal to his long-time agent Bréhier. Her pitch was spirited, but Luchini's love of familiar routine proved unshakeable. See you next time!
Au revoir!
